We have retro_smarts_template (the retrosynthetic direction) and canonical_smarts_template (forward?). The retro_smarts_template is:

'[C:8]-[C@@H;D3;+0:9](-[C@H;D3;+0:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12])-[C@;H0;D4;+0:2](-[C:1])(-[OH;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7])>>[C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7]).[C:8]/[CH;D2;+0:9]=[C;H0;D3;+0:10](/[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12]'

So retrosynthetic template splits product into two fragments: fragment A (left side) is the main chain with OH etc, fragment B is the alkene side.

Thus applying this retro template to the target molecule should give two precursors: the carbonyl fragment and the alkene fragment.

Our target molecule SMILES is given with atom mapping: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

We need to apply retro_smarts_template to this molecule. The apply_template tool likely expects product SMILES and template_id, and will apply retro direction automatically? The earlier apply_template with same template_id returned empty, maybe because it applied forward direction (canonical). We need to specify that we want retro direction. Perhaps we need to use apply_template with the retro_smarts_template directly? But tool expects template_id, not SMARTS. Maybe there is a parameter to indicate direction? Not given.

Alternative: we can manually deduce precursors from the mapping.

From mapped_rxn forward: reactants: ([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1... )=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]) -> product: ([CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]... ) [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])

Thus product is our target. Reactants are two fragments: fragment A: [CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]... )? Wait that's product side? Actually forward reaction: starting from alkene (CH3-CH=CH-...) and carbonyl? Let's parse.

Reactant 1: [CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1... )=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

This is a molecule with a double bond between C:2 (attached to aromatic) and CH:9 (attached to chain). It also has a carbonyl (C:13=O:14) attached to chain and CF3 group.

Reactant 2? Actually the forward reaction only shows one reactant? Wait the forward reaction shows a single reactant with both fragments? The mapping shows product is same as target but with OH instead of carbonyl? Actually product has OH at C:13 and chiral centers.

Thus the forward reaction is a reduction of carbonyl to alcohol and maybe a cyclization? Actually product is a cyclic lactone? Not.

But the retro template splits product into two fragments: one is the carbonyl fragment (C=O) and the other is the alkene fragment.

Thus the precursors are:

Fragment 1 (carbonyl side): [C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F...])... This corresponds to a carbonyl compound: something like CH3-CH(=O)-C(F)3? Let's reconstruct.

From retro_smarts_template left side: [C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F...])... So C:1 is CH3? In mapped_rxn product, CH3 is atom 1 attached to C:2. So fragment is CH3-CH(=O)-C(F)3? Actually C:2 is carbonyl carbon? Wait mapping: In product, C:2 is chiral carbon attached to aromatic and OH? No.

Better to just apply the retro template using tool check_smiles_reaction_template_matching? Not needed.

Maybe apply_template with template_id but need to set direction? Could try apply_template again but maybe need to use the retro_smarts_template ID? The template ID is same; apply_template may apply both forward and retro? It returned empty maybe because product does not match forward side. But maybe we need to set a flag? Not available.

Alternative: we can manually construct precursors using mapping.

From mapped_rxn forward: Reactant (precursor) is: [CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]... )=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Thus the precursor is a single molecule (the same as product but with carbonyl instead of OH and double bond). Wait product is cyclic? Actually product is same as target: [CH3:1][C@H:2]... [C@@:13]1([OH:14])... So product is a cyclic? The product has a ring: [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1... That's a cyclobutane? Actually 5-member ring? Atoms 9-10-11-12-13 form a ring.

Thus the precursor is an open-chain unsaturated carbonyl: [CH3:1]/[C:2]... =[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=O)[C:15](F)(F)F

Thus the precursor is a single molecule (the same as product but with double bond and carbonyl). However the retro template splits into two fragments: the carbonyl fragment (C=O) and the alkene fragment (C=CH-...). Wait the retro template shows product -> two fragments: one is carbonyl fragment (C:1 - C:2(=O) - C:4(F)3) and the other is alkene fragment [C:8]/[CH;D2;+0:9]=[C;H0;D3;+0:10](/[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12]. So the product is formed by coupling these two fragments.

Thus the precursors are:

Fragment A (alkene): [C:8]/[CH;D2;+0:9]=[C;H0;D3;+0:10](/[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12]

Mapping to our target: C:8 corresponds to CH3? Actually in mapped_rxn product, CH3 is atom 1. In retro template, C:8 is the methyl group attached to the alkene. So fragment A is something like CH3-CH= C(??)-c aromatic? Let's reconstruct using mapping numbers from product.

Our product mapping: atoms:

1 CH2? Actually target has [CH2:1]=[C:2]... So atom 1 is CH2 of double bond. In mapped_rxn product, CH3 is atom 1. Wait discrepancy: In target, the double bond is CH2= C... but in mapped_rxn product, CH3 is attached to C:2. The target seems to be the product after reduction? Let's compare.

Target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1... ) [C@@H:9]1... So there is a double bond between CH2 (1) and C (2). In mapped_rxn product, CH3 is attached to C:2, not double bond. So maybe the target is the product of a different reaction? Actually the target is the product after a retro step? I'm confused.

But the question: "return all possible precursors of applying the template as the result of the task make_1_lvl1-template_search-1 to the molecule below?" So we need to apply the template (ID 1914384) to the given molecule (initial_molecule). The template is the retrosynthetic template (retro_smarts_template). So we need to get precursors.

Thus we need to apply retro_smarts_template to the target molecule. Since tool apply_template didn't work, maybe we need to use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching to see if it matches. But we need actual precursors.

We can manually derive using the mapping from the forward reaction: The product is the target molecule (the one with OH). The precursors are the two fragments shown on the right side of retro_smarts_template: the carbonyl fragment and the alkene fragment.

Let's extract their SMILES using the mapping numbers.

From retro_smarts_template right side:

Fragment 1: [C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7])

Replace with actual atoms from product mapping:

C:1 corresponds to atom with mapping 1 in product: In product mapping, atom 1 is CH2? Actually product mapping: [CH2:1]=[C:2]... So C:1 is CH2 (sp2). But in fragment, C:1 is a carbon attached to C:2 (the carbonyl carbon). In product, the carbonyl carbon is C:13? Wait product has OH at C:13, carbonyl is gone. So mapping may not align.

Maybe the mapping numbers in retro template correspond to product mapping numbers, which are same as in mapped_rxn product. In mapped_rxn product, atoms 1-18 correspond to product. So we can map:

- C:1 = atom 1 (CH3) in product? In mapped_rxn product, atom 1 is CH3 attached to C:2. Indeed product has CH3 attached to C:2 (the chiral carbon). In our target, we have CH2 double bond to C:2, not CH3. So maybe the target is not the same as product of that reaction. Wait the target is [CH2:1]=[C:2]... So atom 1 is CH2, not CH3. So the mapping numbers differ.

Thus maybe the target is the product of a different reaction, not the same as mapped_rxn product. The template may still apply but with different mapping.

Given complexity, perhaps the tool apply_template should have returned precursors but returned empty due to mismatch. Could be that the template does not apply to this molecule, meaning no precursors. In that case answer is empty list [].

But the question expects some list.
